q: 1. For calculating the depth of an isolated sloped footing of width "b" for a column of size "a", the width of the footing is taken as ...........
explain: This is a simplified geometric approximation used for determining effective width in sloped footing calculations.

q: 2. The zone in which transverse bending is likely to occur may be obtained by drawing a line from the faces to the column making an angle 'θ' with the horizontal where 'θ' may be ...........
explain: A 45-degree dispersion is commonly assumed for the distribution of loads and stresses in thick concrete elements like footings.

q: 3. A square column of side a is founded on a square footing is side b. The maximum bending moment on the footing corresponding to a net upward pressure p is given by ...........
explain: Derived from treating the cantilever portion of the footing as a beam: $M =  rac{p \cdot ( rac{b-a}{2})^2}{2}$ per unit width.

q: 4. A compression member is termed as column or strut if the ratio of its effective length to the least lateral dimension is more than ...........
explain: If the slenderness ratio (Le/d) is less than 3, the member is considered a pedestal rather than a column.

q: 5. All columns shall be designed for an eccentricity not less than ...........
explain: Even if a column is nominally axially loaded, a minimum eccentricity of 20 mm must be considered to account for construction tolerances.

q: 6. When a vertical member is carrying mainly axial loads, it is termed as a ...........
explain: While 'strut' is a general term for compression members, 'column' specifically refers to vertical compression members in buildings.

q: 7. The shape of a column should be ...........
explain: Columns can be designed in any shape (square, rectangle, circle, L-shape, T-shape) depending on the architectural and structural needs.

q: 8. When the ratio of effective length of the column to its least lateral dimension does not exceed 12, it is termed as a ...........
explain: A column is classified as short if its slenderness ratio (Le/d) is 12 or less (Note: some older texts used 15, but 12 is the standard).

q: 9. While designing a reinforced concrete pole as a column, it is considered as ...........
options: fixed at one end and hinged at the other end
explain: R.C.C. poles are generally embedded deep in the ground, providing a fixed-end condition at the base and continuity at the top.

q: 10. The purpose of lateral ties in short reinforced concrete columns is to ...........
options: increase the load carrying capacity of the column
explain: Lateral ties provide lateral support to the longitudinal bars to prevent them from buckling outward under high axial loads.

q: 11. A long column is one whose ratio of effective length to its least lateral dimension exceeds ...........
explain: If the ratio of effective length to least lateral dimension (Le/d) exceeds 12, it is classified as a long (slender) column.

q: 12. In a column, with helical reinforcement, the permissible load is based on the core area. The least lateral dimension of such a column should be taken as ...........
options: equal to the diameter of core
explain: In a helically reinforced column, the 'core' is the concrete area enclosed within the center-line of the helical reinforcement, and its diameter defines the least lateral dimension for specific calculations.

q: 13. The area of longitudinal steel reinforcement in a column should not be ...........
options: less than 0.8% of the area of concrete section required for direct load alone
more than 6% of the gross sectional are of column
explain: IS:456 mandates a minimum of 0.8% (to prevent buckling and shrinkage cracks) and a maximum of 6% (to avoid congestion, though 4% is preferred for practical casting).

q: 14. The diameter of the polygonal links or lateral ties should not be less than....... of the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar ...........
explain: To provide adequate lateral restraint, the tie diameter must be at least one-fourth (1/4) the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar.

q: 15. The diameter of lateral ties, in no case, shall be less than ...........
explain: Regardless of the longitudinal bar size, the minimum absolute diameter for lateral ties is 5 mm (often rounded to 6 mm or 8 mm in modern practice).

q: 16. For a longitudinal reinforcing bar in a column, the cover should not be less than ...........
explain: A clear cover of 40 mm is required for columns to protect the steel from corrosion and fire, or the diameter of the bar if it is larger than 40 mm.

q: 17. A compression member is considered as short when both the slenderness ratio lex/D and ley/b are less than ...........
explain: A column is classified as short if the ratio of effective length to the corresponding lateral dimension is less than 12.

q: 18. The effective length of column with one and effectively held in position and other restrained against rotation at both directions is ...........
explain: For a column with both ends fixed against rotation and position, the theoretical value is 0.5l, but the design (recommended) value is 0.65l.

q: 19. The effective length of a column with both ends effectively held in position, but not restrained against rotation is ...........
explain: For a column with both ends hinged (held in position but free to rotate), the effective length is equal to the unsupported length 'l'.

q: 20. A column is regarded as long column if the ration of its effective length to least lateral radius of gyration is more than ...........
explain: A slenderness ratio (l/r) greater than 60 indicates a long column likely to fail by buckling before reaching its crushing strength.

q: 21. The minimum eccentricity that should be used in the design of any R.C.C. column is given by ...........
explain: IS:456 specifies emin = (L/500) + (D/30), but not less than 20 mm, to account for misalignments.

q: 22. The minimum percentage of longitudinal reinforcement in R.C.C. columns is ...........
explain: A minimum of 0.8% steel is necessary to help handle accidental eccentricity and shrinkage stresses in the concrete.

q: 23. The maximum percentage of longitudinal reinforcement in R.C.C. columns is ...........
explain: Though 4% is common in practice to allow for lapping, the maximum theoretical limit is 6.0% of the gross cross-sectional area.

q: 24. The minimum diameter of longitudinal reinforcement in R.C.C. column should not be less than ...........
explain: Main longitudinal bars in a column must have a minimum diameter of 12 mm to ensure sufficient stiffness for the cage.

q: 25. The minimum accidental eccentricity in axially loaded columns may occur due to ...........
explain: Accidental eccentricity accounts for construction defects, non-homogeneity of concrete, and uncertainty in end fixation.

q: 26. Transverse reinforcement in columns ...........
explain: Ties/links primarily prevent buckling of the main bars and confine the core; they are not directly accounted for in axial load capacity calculations.

q: 27. A column is a structural element that supports axial compression load and has a height equal t at least ...........
explain: By definition, if the ratio of the effective length to the least lateral dimension is less than 3, it's a pedestal, not a column.

q: 28. The effective length of column is taken as ...........
options: the distance between the ends of column
twice the length between ends of column
the half length between the ends of column
the distance between the points of contra flexure
explain: The effective length (Le) is the distance between adjacent points of zero moment (points of contraflexure) in the buckling shape.

q: 29. The ratio of minimum area of cross section of longitudinal bars and gross sectional area of column shall be ...........
explain: Since the minimum percentage is 0.8%, this corresponds to 0.8/100, which simplifies to 1/125.

q: 30. To provide sufficient rigidity in the column while fixing and concreting, the reinforced bars should not be less than ...........
explain: Bars smaller than 12 mm lack the structural rigidity required to withstand the forces of concrete pouring and vibration without shifting.

q: 31. The ratio of minimum number of longitudinal bars provided in rectangular columns to those in circular column is ...........
explain: Rectangular columns require a minimum of 4 bars (one in each corner), while circular columns require a minimum of 6 bars. The ratio is 4/6, which simplifies to 2/3.

q: 32. Spacing of longitudinal bars measured along the peripheral of the column should not exceed ...........
explain: As per IS 456, the maximum spacing between longitudinal bars along the periphery of the column is limited to 300 mm to prevent local buckling of the concrete face.

q: 33. The nominal longitudinal reinforcement in pedestals should not be less than ...........
explain: For pedestals (where length is less than 3 times the least lateral dimension), the minimum longitudinal reinforcement is 0.15% of the gross cross-sectional area.

q: 34. A pedestal is said to be a compression member when its effective length does not exceed ...........
options: two times the least lateral dimension
three times the least lateral dimension
four times the least lateral dimension
explain: A vertical compression member is classified as a pedestal if its effective length is less than or equal to 3 times its least lateral dimension.

q: 35. The internal angle of laterals ties in the form of polygonal links in columns shall not exceed ...........
explain: To ensure effective lateral restraint and prevent the tie from 'opening' under pressure, the internal angle of a polygonal link should not exceed 135°.

q: 36. The diameter of the helical reinforcement should not be less than X-times the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar subject to a minimum of 5 mm, where X is ...........
explain: The diameter of transverse or helical reinforcement must be at least one-fourth (1/4) the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar, with a minimum of 5 mm (or 6mm in modern practice).

q: 37. All compression members are designed for minimum eccentricity equal to ...........
options: unsupported length of column/500 plus lateral dimension/30 subject to a minimum of 20 mm
unsupported length of column/400 plus lateral dimension/30 subject to a minimum of 20 mm
supported length of column/500 plus lateral dimension/30 subject to a minimum of 20 mm
unsupported length of column/400 plus lateral dimension/30 subject to a minimum of 20 mm
explain: IS 456 defines minimum eccentricity as (L/500) + (D/30), where L is unsupported length and D is lateral dimension, but it cannot be less than 20 mm.

q: 38. The minimum number of longitudinal steel bars in R.C.C. rectangular columns must be ...........
explain: Every corner of a rectangular or square column must have a bar to provide symmetrical reinforcement and tie the cage, necessitating at least 4 bars.

q: 39. The minimum number of longitudinal steel bars in R.C.C. circular columns must be ...........
explain: For circular columns, 6 bars are required to properly maintain the circular shape of the reinforcement cage and provide uniform confinement.

q: 40. The minimum number of longitudinal steel bars in helically reinforced R.C.C. columns must be ...........
explain: Helical reinforcement is typically used in circular columns, which requires a minimum of 6 longitudinal bars for stability of the helix.

q: 41. Spacing of longitudinal bars measured along the periphery of a circular R.C.C. column shall not exceed ...........
explain: The 300 mm maximum spacing rule applies to all column shapes, including circular ones, to ensure the concrete surface is effectively reinforced.

q: 42. The maximum spacing of longitudinal bars with a tie bent around alternate bars in R.C.C columns is ...........
explain: If bars are not effectively tied (i.e., the tie only wraps alternate bars), the maximum distance between a tied bar and an untied bar is 150 mm.

q: 43. The spacing of the longitudinal bars effectively tied should not exceed the following if additional longitudinal bars provided in between are tied in one direction by open ties ...........
explain: Specific detailing requirements for secondary ties/links often relate spacing to the diameter of the transverse reinforcement (48 times the tie diameter).

q: 44. The diameter of transverse reinforcement of columns should be equal to one fourth of the diameter of the main rods but not less than ...........
explain: While 5mm was the older standard, current practice (and many code versions) specifies a 6 mm minimum for transverse ties to ensure cage rigidity.

q: 45. The spacing of transverse reinforcement of a column shall not be more than ...........
options: the least lateral dimension of a column
sixteen times the smallest diameter of the longitudinal reinforcement bar to be tied
forty-eight times the diameter of the transverse reinforcement
explain: IS 456 pitch requirements for ties: Spacing should be the least of: 1) Least lateral dimension, 2) 16x smallest longitudinal bar diameter, or 3) 48x tie diameter.

q: 46. If the size of a column is reduced above the floor, the main bars of the column are ...........
options: bent inward at the floor level
stopped just below the floor level and separate bars are provided
explain: Bars can be cranked (bent) inward if the offset is small (slope 1 in 6); otherwise, they are terminated and new starter bars are lapped.

q: 47. An additional longitudinal reinforcement in webs of beams should be placed if the depth of the web is more than 750 mm at
explain: Side face reinforcement is required in deep beams (web > 750mm) to control cracking due to shrinkage and temperature.

q: 48. The minimum number of torsional longitudinal reinforcement bars to be provided in R.C.C. beams is
explain: At least one longitudinal bar must be placed in each corner of the stirrups to resist torsion, total of 4 bars.

q: 49. For bridge slabs, the amount of transverse reinforcement is taken as
explain: Specific codes for bridges often require higher distribution steel, typically 0.3% of the gross area.

q: 50. The minimum lap length at the splice of compression reinforcement in a R.C.C member should be more than
options: 30 times the diameter of the bar
twice the development length or 30 times the diameter of the bar
48 times the diameter of the bar
24 times the diameter of the bar or development length
explain: In compression, the lap length is equal to the development length in compression but not less than 24φ.
